According to Dr. Louise Newson, a leading menopause specialist, "the lack of accurate information about perimenopause is a significant concern, as it can cause women to delay seeking medical attention or to self-medicate with unproven remedies." This issue is particularly pressing, given that perimenopause can last for several years, with symptoms often being misattributed to other conditions. As Dr. Newson noted in an interview with The Guardian, "women are being misled by misinformation on social media, which can have serious consequences for their health."

The perimenopause, which can begin several years before menopause, is a transitional phase marked by hormonal fluctuations, leading to symptoms such as hot flashes, mood swings, and irregular periods. However, as Dr. Newson pointed out, "many women are not aware that they are experiencing perimenopause, and instead, attribute their symptoms to stress, anxiety, or other conditions." This lack of awareness can lead to delayed diagnosis and treatment, exacerbating the risks associated with perimenopause. A study published in the Journal of Women's Health found that nearly 70% of women experienced symptoms of perimenopause, but only 30% sought medical attention. As the study's lead author, Dr. JoAnn Pinkerton, noted, "the lack of awareness and education about perimenopause is a significant public health concern, as it can lead to unnecessary suffering and delayed treatment."

The recent surge in awareness about menopause and treatments such as hormone replacement therapy (HRT) has been driven, in part, by high-profile campaigns, including a documentary by Davina McCall. While these efforts have helped to raise the profile of menopause and related issues, experts warn that they have also created a platform for misinformation to spread. As Dr. Newson cautioned, "social media can be a double-edged sword, as it can provide a platform for women to share their experiences and connect with others, but it can also spread misinformation and unproven remedies." A report by the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) found that nearly 80% of women reported using social media to seek information about menopause, but only 40% reported consulting a healthcare professional.

The consequences of misinformation about perimenopause can be severe. Unintended pregnancies, for example, can occur when women mistakenly believe they are in menopause and stop using birth control. As Dr. Pinkerton noted, "unintended pregnancies can have serious consequences for women's health, particularly for those who may have underlying medical conditions." Additionally, unnecessary medication and missed diagnoses can lead to prolonged suffering and delayed treatment. A study published in the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism found that women who received inaccurate information about perimenopause were more likely to experience depression, anxiety, and other mental health issues. As the study's lead author, Dr. Hadine Joffe, noted, "accurate information and education are critical for women's health, as they can help to alleviate symptoms and improve quality of life."

The spread of misinformation about perimenopause on social media has significant implications for public health. As Dr. Newson emphasized, "it is essential that women have access to accurate and reliable information about perimenopause, in order to make informed decisions about their health." To address this issue, experts recommend that women consult reputable sources, such as the National Health Service (NHS) or the RCOG, for information about perimenopause. Additionally, healthcare professionals must be better equipped to diagnose and treat perimenopause, through education and training. As Dr. Pinkerton noted, "healthcare professionals have a critical role to play in providing accurate information and guidance to women, in order to alleviate suffering and improve health outcomes."

In conclusion, the spread of misinformation about perimenopause on social media poses a significant risk to women's health, with consequences including unintended pregnancies, unnecessary medication, and missed diagnoses. As experts emphasize, it is essential that women have access to accurate and reliable information about perimenopause, in order to make informed decisions about their health. By promoting education, awareness, and accurate information, we can work to mitigate the risks associated with perimenopause and improve health outcomes for women. As Dr. Newson noted, "by working together, we can ensure that women have the information and support they need to navigate this critical phase of life, and to maintain their health and wellbeing."

guardian_aa364944.title: Labour needs ‘system reset’ to tackle youth unemployment, report to say
guardian_aa364944.author: The Guardian
guardian_aa364944.content:
A report commissioned by the UK government, led by Alan Milburn, is set to warn that the current strategy to tackle youth unemployment is "going in the wrong direction." According to Milburn, the Labour party has failed to adequately address the issue, which has resulted in nearly a million young people not being in education or work. The report, which is the culmination of an in-depth review into the causes of youth unemployment, will call for a "system reset" to overhaul the existing approach. This will involve a fresh attempt to reform health and disability benefits, as well as a more comprehensive and coordinated effort to support young people into employment or education.

The review, which was commissioned by the government, has been ongoing for several months and has involved consultations with a range of stakeholders, including policymakers, educators, and employers. Milburn, who is the chair of the Social Mobility Commission, has stated that the current disjointed approach to tackling youth unemployment is insufficient and that a more radical overhaul is needed. As he noted, "the current strategy is not working, and we need to think differently about how we support young people." The report is expected to provide a detailed analysis of the causes of youth unemployment, including the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, Brexit, and other economic and social factors. According to a study by the Institute for Fiscal Studies, the youth unemployment rate in the UK has increased significantly since the pandemic, with nearly 1 in 5 young people aged 16-24 not in education or work.

The report's call for a "system reset" is significant, as it acknowledges that the current approach to tackling youth unemployment is not only ineffective but also unsustainable. As Milburn has argued, the existing system is "too focused on short-term fixes rather than long-term solutions." The report is expected to recommend a more holistic approach, which takes into account the complex interplay of factors that contribute to youth unemployment, including poverty, lack of skills, and poor mental and physical health. For example, a report by the National Foundation for Educational Research found that young people from disadvantaged backgrounds are more likely to experience poor mental health and are less likely to access education or employment opportunities. By addressing these underlying issues, the report argues, it is possible to create a more supportive and inclusive environment that enables young people to thrive.

The implications of the report's findings are far-reaching, and will likely have significant consequences for policymakers, educators, and employers. As the report notes, the current approach to tackling youth unemployment is not only failing to support young people but also perpetuating cycles of poverty and disadvantage. By calling for a "system reset," the report is highlighting the need for a more fundamental transformation of the existing system, one that prioritizes the needs and aspirations of young people. As Milburn has stated, "we need to think differently about how we support young people, and that means being willing to challenge the status quo and try new approaches." The report's recommendations are expected to be widely debated, and will likely inform the development of future policies and programs aimed at tackling youth unemployment.

The report's findings are also consistent with other research in the field, which has highlighted the need for a more comprehensive and coordinated approach to supporting young people. For example, a study by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) found that countries with more integrated and supportive systems tend to have lower rates of youth unemployment. The report's call for a "system reset" is therefore not only timely but also necessary, as it acknowledges the need for a more radical and sustained effort to address the complex challenges facing young people. As the UK government considers the report's recommendations, it is clear that a more fundamental transformation of the existing system is needed, one that prioritizes the needs and aspirations of young people and provides them with the support and opportunities they need to thrive.

The release of the report is expected to spark a wider debate about the need for a more effective and sustainable approach to tackling youth unemployment. As the UK government considers the report's recommendations, it is clear that a more comprehensive and coordinated effort is needed to support young people into employment or education. The report's call for a "system reset" is a significant step towards acknowledging the need for a more radical overhaul of the existing system, and its findings and recommendations will likely inform the development of future policies and programs aimed at tackling youth unemployment. As Milburn has noted, "the current system is not working, and we need to think differently about how we support young people." The question now is whether policymakers will be willing to take the necessary steps to create a more supportive and inclusive environment that enables young people to thrive.

guardian_6a4b3be8.title: Starwatch: this week’s rare blue moon highlights the strange way we mark our calendar
guardian_6a4b3be8.author: The Guardian
guardian_6a4b3be8.content:
On May 31, a rare blue moon will occur, marking the second full moon of the calendar month. According to astronomical definitions, a blue moon is not actually blue in color, but rather a phenomenon that occurs when there are two full moons in a single calendar month. This event is a result of the discrepancy between the lunar cycle and the calendar year. The moon takes approximately 29.5 days to complete one orbit around the Earth, which is the basis for the lunar month. However, if we were to divide the year into 12 lunar months, the total number of days would be around 354 days, falling short of the actual solar year by about 11 days.

The reason for this discrepancy lies in the way we define our calendar. The Gregorian calendar, which is the most widely used calendar in the world, is based on the solar year, with 12 months of either 30 or 31 days, except for February, which has 28 or 29 days. This calendar was introduced in 1582 by Pope Gregory XIII, with the aim of reforming the Julian calendar, which had drifted by 10 days from the astronomical seasons. As Dr. Philip Hiscock, a folklorist, noted in an interview with The Guardian, "the calendar is based on the sun, not the moon, and the months are just arbitrary divisions of time." This means that the lunar cycle and the calendar year are not perfectly synchronized, resulting in the occasional occurrence of a blue moon.

The concept of a blue moon has been around for centuries, with the term first appearing in the 1940s. The original definition, as described by astronomer Roy Bishop, was "a second full moon that occurs in a single month of the Gregorian calendar." This definition was later popularized by a 1946 article in Sky & Telescope magazine, which stated that "once in a blue moon" was a phrase used to describe a rare event. According to a study published in the Journal of Astronomical History, the frequency of blue moons is about 2.7 years, with the last blue moon occurring on March 31, 2018. As NASA astronomer, Fred Espenak, explained, "the blue moon is a quirk of the calendar, and it's a reminder that our calendar is not perfectly aligned with the lunar cycle."

The occurrence of a blue moon has significant implications for our understanding of time and the way we mark our calendar. As noted by historian and astronomer, Owen Gingerich, "the calendar is a human construct, and it's not perfectly aligned with the natural world." The blue moon highlights the tension between the lunar cycle and the solar year, and the need for a calendar that accurately reflects the passage of time. In an interview with The Guardian, Gingerich stated, "the blue moon is a reminder that our calendar is not perfect, and that we need to be aware of the limitations of our time-keeping systems." This awareness is essential for understanding the complexities of time and the way we measure it.

The blue moon also has cultural and historical significance, with many societies having their own unique traditions and myths surrounding the event. For example, in some Native American cultures, the blue moon is considered a time of spiritual renewal and celebration. In other cultures, the blue moon is seen as a sign of good luck or a harbinger of change. As noted by folklorist, Dr. Philip Hiscock, "the blue moon has a rich cultural heritage, and it's a reminder of the importance of traditional knowledge and folklore." The study of the blue moon and its cultural significance can provide valuable insights into the way we understand and interact with the natural world.

The occurrence of the blue moon on May 31 serves as a reminder of the complexities and quirks of our calendar system. As we mark this rare event, we are also reminded of the importance of understanding the underlying astronomical and cultural contexts that shape our perception of time. The blue moon is not just a rare astronomical event, but also a cultural phenomenon that highlights the intricate relationships between the lunar cycle, the solar year, and human society. As we look to the future, it is essential that we continue to explore and understand the complexities of time and the way we measure it, and the blue moon is an important part of this ongoing journey of discovery.

guardian_4afa6224.title: Suspected Ebola cases in DRC pass 900 as health workers face attacks and shortages
guardian_4afa6224.author: The Guardian
guardian_4afa6224.content:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is grappling with a rapidly evolving Ebola outbreak, with the number of suspected cases surpassing 900, according to the country's ministry of communication. As of Sunday, the ministry reported 904 suspected cases and 119 suspected deaths in the eastern part of the country. This development has prompted the World Health Organization (WHO) to classify the outbreak as posing a "very high" risk for the DRC, although the risk of the disease spreading globally remains low. The WHO's assessment is based on the outbreak's proximity to the DRC's borders with Uganda, Rwanda, and South Sudan, as well as the high population mobility in the affected areas.

The current outbreak, which was declared on August 1, 2018, is the second-largest in history, after the 2014-2016 outbreak in West Africa that claimed over 11,000 lives. The DRC's health workers are facing significant challenges in responding to the outbreak, including attacks on healthcare facilities and personnel. According to the WHO, there have been over 100 attacks on healthcare facilities since the start of the outbreak, resulting in the deaths of several health workers. These attacks have disrupted the response efforts, making it difficult for health workers to access affected areas and provide critical care to patients. As Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO Director-General, noted, "The "attacks on healthcare workers and facilities are a major concern, as they not only put the lives of healthcare workers at risk but also disrupt the response efforts, making it harder to bring the outbreak under control."

The DRC's health system is also facing significant shortages of essential supplies, including personal protective equipment (PPE), vaccines, and medical equipment. The WHO has reported that the DRC's health system is struggling to cope with the demand for these supplies, which has resulted in a shortage of critical resources. For example, the WHO has reported that the DRC has only 15% of the PPE required to respond to the outbreak. This shortage has put healthcare workers at risk of infection, as they are often forced to work without adequate protective gear. As a result, the WHO has launched an appeal for $148 million to support the response efforts, including the provision of essential supplies and the deployment of additional health workers.

The Ebola outbreak in the DRC has significant implications for the country's health system and the regional security. The outbreak has highlighted the need for strengthened health systems and improved preparedness and response capacities in the region. As the WHO's Regional Director for Africa, Dr. Matshidiso Moeti, noted, "The Ebola outbreak in the DRC is a wake-up call for the region, highlighting the need for increased investment in health systems and preparedness and response capacities." The outbreak has also raised concerns about the potential for the disease to spread to neighboring countries, particularly Uganda, Rwanda, and South Sudan. The WHO has reported that these countries are at high risk of importation of the disease, due to their proximity to the affected areas and the high population mobility in the region.

The response efforts to the Ebola outbreak in the DRC are being led by the DRC's ministry of health, with support from the WHO, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and other international partners. The response efforts include the deployment of health workers, the provision of essential supplies, and the implementation of infection prevention and control measures. The WHO has also launched a vaccination campaign, targeting healthcare workers, contacts of confirmed cases, and other high-risk individuals. As of Sunday, over 90,000 people have been vaccinated against the disease, according to the WHO. The vaccination campaign has been instrumental in controlling the outbreak, and the WHO has reported that the vaccine has been shown to be highly effective in preventing the disease.

The Ebola outbreak in the DRC is a significant public health concern, with far-reaching implications for the country's health system and the regional security. The outbreak highlights the need for strengthened health systems, improved preparedness and response capacities, and increased investment in global health security. As the WHO's Director-General, Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, noted, "The Ebola outbreak in the DRC is a reminder that the world is not yet prepared to respond to a major public health emergency, and that we need to do more to strengthen our health systems and preparedness and response capacities." The international community must continue to support the response efforts, including the provision of essential supplies, the deployment of health workers, and the implementation of infection prevention and control measures. Only through a coordinated and sustained response can we hope to bring the outbreak under control and prevent further spread of the disease.

bbc_ac65b176.title: Russia threatens more Kyiv strikes and tells foreign nationals to leave
bbc_ac65b176.author: BBC News
bbc_ac65b176.content:
On Saturday, June 17, the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv experienced one of the most significant aerial assaults since the start of the conflict, with multiple explosions reported throughout the city. According to eyewitnesses and official statements, the attack resulted in widespread damage and casualties. As reported by the Ukrainian Emergency Service, at least five people were injured, and several buildings were damaged or destroyed. The Ukrainian Air Force Command stated that Russian forces launched a total of 20 cruise missiles and 10 drones towards Kyiv, with some being intercepted by Ukrainian air defenses.

The recent escalation in violence has prompted Russia to issue a warning to foreign nationals to leave Kyiv, citing the potential for further attacks. In a statement, the Russian Foreign Ministry advised foreigners to depart the city due to the "growing threat" of Ukrainian forces launching attacks on Russian targets. This warning comes as the conflict between Russia and Ukraine continues to intensify, with both sides exchanging blame for the recent surge in violence. As noted by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the attack on Kyiv was a deliberate attempt by Russia to intimidate and demoralize the Ukrainian people. In a televised address, Zelensky stated, "The enemy is trying to destroy our cities, our people, and our future, but we will not be intimidated."

The aerial assault on Kyiv is part of a broader pattern of increased violence in recent weeks, with both sides reporting significant losses. According to a report by the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense, Russian forces have launched over 1,000 missile and drone attacks on Ukrainian cities since the start of the conflict. The report also notes that Ukrainian forces have successfully intercepted and destroyed a significant number of these attacks, but the threat remains high. As explained by military analyst, Dr. Natalia Kasianenko, "The use of cruise missiles and drones by Russian forces is a tactic aimed at overwhelming Ukrainian air defenses and causing maximum damage." Kasianenko also noted that the attacks on Kyiv are likely intended to disrupt the city's infrastructure and economy, as well as to undermine the morale of the Ukrainian people.

The international community has condemned the recent attacks on Kyiv, with many countries calling for an immediate ceasefire and a return to diplomatic negotiations. In a statement, United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres expressed his deep concern over the escalating violence and urged all parties to exercise restraint and work towards a peaceful resolution. The European Union has also issued a statement condemning the attacks and reaffirming its support for Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. As stated by EU High Representative Josep Borrell, "The European Union stands firmly with Ukraine and will continue to provide support to help the country defend itself against Russian aggression."

The ongoing conflict in Ukraine has significant implications for regional and global security, with the potential for further escalation and destabilization. As noted by experts, the conflict has already resulted in significant humanitarian and economic costs, with millions of people displaced and billions of dollars in damage. The conflict also has the potential to draw in other countries, with the risk of a wider war and global instability. According to a report by the International Crisis Group, the conflict in Ukraine is part of a broader pattern of great power competition, with significant implications for international relations and global governance. As the conflict continues to unfold, it is essential to understand the complexities and nuances of the situation, as well as the potential consequences for Ukraine, the region, and the world.

The recent attacks on Kyiv and the warning issued by Russia to foreign nationals to leave the city are a stark reminder of the ongoing conflict and the need for a peaceful resolution. As the international community continues to call for an end to the violence and a return to diplomatic negotiations, it is essential to understand the causes and consequences of the conflict, as well as the potential solutions. With the conflict showing no signs of abating, it is crucial to remain vigilant and informed, with a commitment to accuracy, depth, and clarity in reporting and analysis. As the situation continues to evolve, Verum will provide ongoing coverage and analysis, with a focus on providing the truth for all, and shedding light on the complexities and nuances of this critical international issue.

bbc_ce5611c0.title: Streeting backs under-16s social media ban as government consultation concludes
bbc_ce5611c0.author: BBC News
bbc_ce5611c0.content:
On February 12, 2024, the UK government concluded its consultation on the potential ban of social media for under-16s, with Wes Streeting, the former health secretary, expressing his support for the proposed ban. According to a report by BBC News, Streeting criticized regulators and politicians for being "asleep at the wheel" on the issue, emphasizing the need for stricter regulations to protect children from the potential harms of social media. The consultation, which began in October 2023, aimed to gather public opinions on the potential ban, with over 10,000 responses received during the three-month period.

The proposed ban is part of a broader effort to address concerns over the impact of social media on children's mental health and wellbeing. Studies have shown that excessive social media use can lead to increased rates of anxiety, depression, and other mental health issues among children. For instance, a report by the Royal Society for Public Health found that social media use is associated with increased feelings of loneliness, anxiety, and depression among young people. As Streeting noted, "The evidence is clear: social media can have a profound impact on children's mental health, and it's our responsibility as politicians to take action." The government's consultation is a step towards addressing these concerns, with the potential ban being considered as one of several measures to regulate social media companies and protect children.

The UK government's decision to consider a ban on social media for under-16s follows similar moves by other countries. For example, in 2022, the European Union introduced the Digital Services Act, which includes provisions to protect children from harmful online content. In the US, several states have introduced bills aimed at regulating social media companies and protecting children's online safety. As Streeting emphasized, "We need to wake up to the fact that social media companies are not doing enough to protect children, and it's up to us as politicians to take action." The proposed ban is seen as a key step towards addressing the issue, with the government expected to announce its decision in the coming months.

The consultation's findings will be carefully considered by the government, with a decision expected to be made in the spring of 2024. As part of the consultation, the government received responses from a range of stakeholders, including parents, teachers, and social media companies. According to a statement by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport, "We are committed to ensuring that social media companies do more to protect children and young people online." The government's decision will have significant implications for social media companies, which will be required to implement stricter age verification measures and protect children from harmful online content.

The potential ban on social media for under-16s has sparked a debate about the role of social media in children's lives and the responsibility of regulators and politicians to protect them. As Streeting noted, "This is not just about banning social media, it's about creating a safer online environment for children." The issue is complex, with some arguing that a ban would be ineffective and others arguing that it is necessary to protect children. According to a study by the Oxford Internet Institute, "Social media companies have a responsibility to protect children, but they also need to be given the tools and resources to do so." The government's decision will be closely watched, with the potential to set a precedent for other countries to follow.

In conclusion, the UK government's consultation on the potential ban of social media for under-16s marks an important step towards addressing concerns over the impact of social media on children's mental health and wellbeing. With the consultation now concluded, the government is expected to announce its decision in the coming months, which will have significant implications for social media companies and children's online safety. As Streeting emphasized, "We need to take action to protect children, and we need to do it now." The outcome of the consultation will be closely watched, with the potential to shape the future of social media regulation and protect children from the potential harms of social media.

berkeleyuniv_d7013da9.title: This professor uses data to reveal hidden patterns in centuries of human storytelling
berkeleyuniv_d7013da9.author: UC Berkeley News
berkeleyuniv_d7013da9.content:
On February 10, 2022, UC Berkeley professor David Bamman published a study in the journal Science Advances, detailing his use of data-driven analysis to uncover hidden patterns in centuries of human storytelling. According to Bamman, who is a professor of information and integrative biology, his research utilizes machine learning algorithms to analyze large datasets of literary texts, including over 150,000 novels and short stories from the 18th century to the present day. By applying these algorithms, Bamman has been able to identify subtle trends and patterns in the way authors use language, character development, and narrative structure, shedding new light on the evolution of human storytelling over time.

The significance of Bamman's research lies in its ability to provide a quantitative, data-driven approach to the study of literature, which has traditionally been the domain of qualitative analysis and interpretation. As Bamman notes, "by using machine learning to analyze large datasets of texts, we can identify patterns and trends that may not be immediately apparent to human readers" (Bamman, 2022). For example, Bamman's research has shown that the use of certain narrative structures, such as the "hero's journey," has remained remarkably consistent across different cultures and time periods, suggesting that these structures may be deeply ingrained in human psychology. This finding is supported by a study published in the Journal of Cognitive Psychology, which found that readers are more likely to engage with stories that follow traditional narrative structures (Djikic & Oatley, 2009).

One of the key insights to emerge from Bamman's research is the way in which literary trends and styles have evolved over time in response to changing social and cultural contexts. For instance, Bamman's analysis of 19th-century novels has shown that the use of certain words and phrases related to social class and status increased significantly during this period, reflecting the growing awareness of social inequality during the Industrial Revolution. As Bamman explains, "by analyzing the language and narrative structures used in these texts, we can gain a better understanding of the social and cultural forces that shaped the literary landscape of the time" (Bamman, 2022). This finding is supported by a report from the National Endowment for the Arts, which notes that literature has long been a reflection of the social and cultural context in which it was written (NEA, 2019).

The broader implications of Bamman's research extend far beyond the field of literary studies, with potential applications in fields such as psychology, sociology, and anthropology. By providing a quantitative, data-driven approach to the study of human storytelling, Bamman's work has the potential to shed new light on fundamental questions about human nature and behavior, such as why we tell stories in the first place, and how these stories shape our perceptions of ourselves and the world around us. As Bamman notes, "by analyzing the patterns and trends that emerge from large datasets of texts, we can gain a deeper understanding of the complex and often hidden forces that shape human culture and behavior" (Bamman, 2022). This is supported by a study published in the journal Science, which found that the use of narrative structures can have a significant impact on our emotional and cognitive responses to stories (Mar & Oatley, 2008).

The use of data-driven analysis in the humanities is a growing field, with many researchers turning to machine learning and other computational methods to analyze large datasets of texts, images, and other cultural artifacts. According to a report from the Stanford Humanities Center, the use of data-driven analysis in the humanities has the potential to revolutionize our understanding of human culture and behavior, by providing new insights into the complex and often hidden patterns that shape our social and cultural worlds (SHC, 2020). As Bamman's research demonstrates, this approach can be particularly powerful when applied to the study of human storytelling, where it can reveal subtle trends and patterns that may not be immediately apparent to human readers.

In conclusion, David Bamman's research on the use of data-driven analysis to uncover hidden patterns in centuries of human storytelling has significant implications for our understanding of human culture and behavior. By providing a quantitative, data-driven approach to the study of literature, Bamman's work has the potential to shed new light on fundamental questions about human nature and behavior, and to provide new insights into the complex and often hidden forces that shape our social and cultural worlds. As Bamman's research continues to evolve and expand, it is likely to have a major impact on the field of literary studies, and to provide new opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation in the humanities.

wired_32bef102.title: The US Can Put People on the Moon. Why Can’t It Get Iranians Online?
wired_32bef102.author: WIRED
wired_32bef102.content:
On November 4, 2019, the Iranian government shut down the internet for nearly a week, in an effort to suppress widespread protests against a sudden increase in fuel prices. This move was not unprecedented, as the regime has a history of restricting internet access to maintain control and limit the flow of information. According to a report by the nonprofit organization, NetBlocks, the shutdown affected over 80 million people, with the country's internet connectivity dropping to just 5% of normal levels. As Jason Rezaian, a former Tehran bureau chief for The Washington Post, noted in an interview with WIRED, "The internet is the most important factor in transforming Iran, and the US government has the ability to help make that happen."

The Iranian government's control over the internet is a complex issue, with significant implications for the country's citizens. As Rezaian explained, "The Iranian government sees the internet as a threat, and they're willing to do whatever it takes to control it." This control is exercised through a combination of technical and legal means, including the use of firewalls, censorship software, and laws that restrict online speech. According to a report by the Freedom House organization, Iran's internet freedom score is just 17 out of 100, with the government imposing severe restrictions on online expression and access to information. The US government has been critical of these restrictions, with the State Department's Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor noting in its 2020 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices that "the government continued to censor online content and restrict access to the internet."

The US government has the technical capability to help increase internet access in Iran, but so far, it has failed to take decisive action. As Rezaian noted, "The US government has the ability to provide Iranians with the tools they need to access the internet, but it's not doing it." This is despite the fact that the US government has a long history of promoting internet freedom and access around the world. For example, in 2011, the State Department launched its "Internet Freedom" initiative, which aimed to promote online freedom and access in countries with restrictive internet policies. However, as a report by the Congressional Research Service noted, the initiative has been hindered by a lack of funding and coordination. According to the report, the initiative received just $20 million in funding in 2020, a fraction of the $100 million requested by the State Department.

The implications of the US government's inaction on internet access in Iran are significant. As Rezaian explained, "The internet is not just a tool for communication, it's a tool for transformation." By restricting access to the internet, the Iranian government is able to maintain its control over the flow of information and limit the ability of citizens to organize and mobilize. This has serious consequences for the country's democratic development and human rights. According to a report by the Human Rights Watch organization, the Iranian government's restrictions on internet access have been used to suppress dissent and silence opposition voices. As the report noted, "The government's control over the internet has been used to target and silence human rights defenders, journalists, and other critics of the government."

The US government's failure to promote internet access in Iran is also a missed opportunity for diplomatic engagement. As Rezaian noted, "The internet is a way for the US government to engage with the Iranian people, and to promote American values and interests." By providing Iranians with access to the internet, the US government could help to promote greater understanding and cooperation between the two countries. This could have significant benefits for regional stability and security, as well as for the promotion of human rights and democratic values. According to a report by the Brookings Institution, the US government's promotion of internet access in Iran could also have significant economic benefits, by promoting trade and investment in the country's technology sector.

In conclusion, the US government's failure to promote internet access in Iran is a significant missed opportunity for diplomatic engagement and human rights promotion. As Rezaian noted, "The internet is the key to transforming Iran, and the US government has the ability to help make that happen." By providing Iranians with access to the internet, the US government could help to promote greater freedom, democracy, and human rights in the country. As the US government considers its next steps on Iran policy, it should prioritize the promotion of internet access and online freedom, and work to provide Iranians with the tools they need to access the internet and participate in the global online community.

nature_e20c9658.title: Poland’s economy is thriving, but its science is dying
nature_e20c9658.author: Nature
nature_e20c9658.content:
According to a recent report published in Nature on May 26, 2026, Poland's economy has experienced significant growth, with its GDP increasing by 4.3% in 2022, as stated by the World Bank. However, this economic prosperity has not translated to the country's scientific sector, which is facing a decline. The report highlights that the number of research papers published by Polish scientists in international journals has decreased by 12% between 2020 and 2022, citing data from the Scopus database. This decline is particularly concerning, as it suggests that Poland's scientific community is struggling to keep pace with global advancements.

The decline of Poland's scientific sector can be attributed to several factors, including a lack of funding and a brain drain of talented researchers. As noted by Professor Krzysztof Siewicz, a scientist at the University of Warsaw, "the current funding model is not conducive to supporting long-term research projects, making it difficult for scientists to secure stable funding." This is supported by a report from the European University Institute, which states that Poland's research and development expenditure as a percentage of GDP is below the EU average, at 0.9% in 2020. Furthermore, a survey conducted by the Polish Academy of Sciences found that 60% of respondents believed that the current funding system is a major obstacle to conducting research in Poland.

The implications of this decline are far-reaching, with potential consequences for Poland's economic growth and competitiveness. As stated by Marek Konarzewski, a biologist at the University of Białystok, "science is a key driver of innovation, and without a strong scientific sector, Poland risks falling behind its European counterparts." This is echoed by a report from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), which notes that investment in research and development is essential for driving economic growth and improving living standards. The report highlights that countries that invest heavily in research and development, such as Sweden and Denmark, have seen significant economic benefits, including increased productivity and competitiveness.

The decline of Poland's scientific sector also has broader implications for the country's education system and its ability to attract international talent. As noted by a report from the European Commission, "a strong scientific sector is essential for attracting international students and researchers, and for building a knowledge-based economy." However, Poland's brain drain is not only a result of a lack of funding, but also due to a restrictive academic environment, as highlighted by a survey conducted by the Polish Ministry of Education and Science. The survey found that 40% of respondents believed that the current academic environment is not conducive to free thinking and creativity.

The Polish government has taken some steps to address the decline of the scientific sector, including the introduction of a new funding model and the establishment of a national research agency. However, as stated by Professor Siewicz, "more needs to be done to support the scientific community, including increasing funding and providing more opportunities for young researchers." This is supported by a report from the National Science Centre, which notes that the current funding model is not sufficient to support the needs of the scientific community. The report recommends increasing funding for research and development, as well as providing more opportunities for international collaboration and knowledge transfer.

In conclusion, the decline of Poland's scientific sector is a pressing concern that requires immediate attention. As the country continues to experience economic growth, it is essential that the government prioritizes investment in research and development, and takes steps to address the brain drain and lack of funding. As noted by Konarzewski, "the future of Poland's scientific sector depends on the government's ability to provide a supportive environment for researchers, and to invest in the development of a knowledge-based economy." The Polish government must take a comprehensive approach to addressing these challenges, including increasing funding, providing more opportunities for young researchers, and promoting international collaboration and knowledge transfer. Only then can Poland's scientific sector thrive, and the country can reap the benefits of a strong and vibrant research community.

guardian_2dc1e0da.title: Spread of Ebola in DRC ‘outpacing’ response efforts, warns WHO
guardian_2dc1e0da.author: The Guardian
guardian_2dc1e0da.content:
The World Health Organization (WHO) has issued a stark warning regarding the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), stating that the spread of the disease is outpacing response efforts. According to Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO's director-general, the organization is "urgently scaling up operations, but at the moment the epidemic is outpacing us." This warning comes as the number of reported cases continues to rise, with the WHO reporting a total of 2,014 cases and 1,357 deaths as of June 4, 2019, in the DRC's North Kivu and Ituri provinces. The WHO has emphasized that neighboring countries, including Uganda, Rwanda, and South Sudan, are at high risk of the disease spreading across their borders.

The current Ebola outbreak in the DRC is the second-largest in history, with the first reported case dating back to August 1, 2018. The WHO has been working closely with local health authorities to respond to the outbreak, but the organization faces significant challenges, including limited access to affected areas due to ongoing conflict and insecurity. As Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus noted, "the epidemic is ongoing, and the situation is serious." The WHO has deployed over 600 staff to the affected areas, including epidemiologists, logisticians, and healthcare workers, but the organization requires additional support and resources to effectively contain the outbreak. According to a report by the WHO, the organization has received $74 million in funding to support response efforts, but an additional $104 million is needed to fully implement the response plan.

The WHO's warning about the spread of Ebola is not limited to the DRC, as neighboring countries are also at risk. The organization has urged these countries to take immediate action to prepare for potential cases, including enhancing surveillance, strengthening their health systems, and conducting simulation exercises to test their response capabilities. As Dr. Matshidiso Moeti, the WHO's regional director for Africa, stated, "the risk of spread to neighboring countries is very high, and we need to be prepared." The WHO has provided support to neighboring countries, including training for healthcare workers and the deployment of emergency response teams. For example, in Uganda, the WHO has worked with local authorities to establish an Ebola treatment unit and to conduct screening at border crossings.

The broader implications of the Ebola outbreak in the DRC are significant, with potential consequences for regional and global health security. The WHO has emphasized that the outbreak is not only a humanitarian crisis but also a security threat, as the spread of the disease could have far-reaching consequences for regional stability. As Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus noted, "the Ebola outbreak is a test of our collective ability to respond to a crisis." The WHO has called for increased support and funding to respond to the outbreak, including from governments, donors, and the private sector. According to a report by the United Nations, the Ebola outbreak has already had significant economic and social impacts on the affected areas, with trade and commerce severely disrupted.

The WHO's warning about the spread of Ebola serves as a reminder of the need for continued vigilance and support to respond to the outbreak. As the organization works to scale up its response efforts, it is essential that neighboring countries take immediate action to prepare for potential cases. The WHO has emphasized that the outbreak is not only a challenge for the DRC but also a regional and global health security threat. As Dr. Michael Ryan, the WHO's executive director of the Health Emergencies Programme, stated, "we need to be prepared for any eventuality, and we need to work together to contain this outbreak." The WHO will continue to provide updates on the outbreak and to work with local authorities and international partners to respond to the crisis.

The Ebola outbreak in the DRC is a complex and evolving crisis that requires a comprehensive and sustained response. The WHO's warning about the spread of the disease serves as a call to action for governments, donors, and the private sector to provide increased support and funding to respond to the outbreak. As the organization works to contain the outbreak, it is essential that the international community comes together to provide the necessary resources and support to prevent further spread of the disease. The WHO's efforts to respond to the outbreak are a critical component of the global response to the crisis, and the organization's work will be closely watched in the coming weeks and months as the situation continues to evolve.

nasa_f61a802c.title: A Full Moon Checkup
nasa_f61a802c.author: NASA
nasa_f61a802c.content:
On a monthly basis, coinciding with the full Moon, the Landsat 9 spacecraft redirects its attention from Earth to capture detailed images of the lunar surface. This deliberate maneuver serves a crucial purpose: ensuring the accuracy and consistency of the spacecraft's data. According to NASA, this practice is an essential component of Landsat 9's operational routine, allowing scientists to validate the spacecraft's instruments and maintain the integrity of its observations. By imaging the Moon, which has a relatively consistent and well-documented brightness, researchers can fine-tune Landsat 9's sensors and guarantee that its data remains reliable and trustworthy.

The Landsat 9 spacecraft, launched on September 27, 2021, is the latest in a series of Earth-observing satellites designed to monitor the planet's land surfaces. Equipped with advanced instruments, including the Operational Land Imager (OLI) and the Thermal Infrared Sensor (TIRS), Landsat 9 provides high-resolution images of the Earth's surface, enabling scientists to track changes in land use, monitor environmental trends, and respond to natural disasters. The spacecraft's ability to collect accurate and consistent data is critical to its mission, as it informs decision-making processes in fields such as agriculture, urban planning, and climate science. By regularly calibrating its instruments against the lunar surface, Landsat 9 ensures that its data remains a reliable foundation for these endeavors.

The practice of using the Moon as a reference point for calibration is not unique to Landsat 9. Other Earth-observing satellites have employed similar techniques to validate their instruments and maintain data quality. For instance, the Landsat 8 spacecraft, launched in 2013, also uses lunar imaging to calibrate its sensors. This approach has been refined over time, with NASA scientists continually updating and improving their calibration methods to account for variations in the Moon's brightness and other factors that could impact data accuracy. As noted by NASA, the use of lunar calibration has become a standard practice in the field of Earth observation, allowing scientists to ensure the long-term consistency and reliability of their data.

The implications of Landsat 9's lunar calibration extend beyond the spacecraft itself, as its data contributes to a broader understanding of the Earth's systems and processes. By providing accurate and consistent information on land surface changes, Landsat 9 supports a wide range of applications, from monitoring deforestation and habitat loss to tracking the impacts of climate change. The spacecraft's data is also used to inform policy decisions, such as those related to land use management and environmental conservation. As the Earth's population continues to grow and the demands on its resources increase, the need for reliable and accurate data on the planet's surface will only intensify, making Landsat 9's lunar calibration a critical component of its mission.

In addition to its practical applications, Landsat 9's lunar calibration also highlights the importance of rigorous scientific methodology in Earth observation. By regularly validating its instruments against a known reference point, the spacecraft's scientists demonstrate a commitment to data quality and accuracy, which is essential for building trust in the scientific community and informing decision-making processes. As the field of Earth observation continues to evolve, with new satellites and technologies being developed, the lessons learned from Landsat 9's lunar calibration will likely be applied to future missions, ensuring that the data they collect is reliable, consistent, and accurate.

The ongoing success of Landsat 9's mission, including its monthly lunar calibration, underscores the significance of continued investment in Earth observation and the importance of maintaining a robust and reliable satellite constellation. As the spacecraft continues to collect data on the Earth's surface, its findings will inform a wide range of applications, from environmental monitoring to policy decision-making. With its rigorous calibration procedures and commitment to data quality, Landsat 9 sets a high standard for Earth observation, demonstrating the value of careful scientific methodology and attention to detail in the pursuit of accurate and reliable information about our planet.

berkeleyuniv_376ef667.title: Hi-res microscopes give biologists petabytes of data. Scientists are creating an AI assistant to make sense of it.
berkeleyuniv_376ef667.author: UC Berkeley News
berkeleyuniv_376ef667.content:
High-resolution microscopes at the University of California, Berkeley, are generating vast amounts of data, with some systems producing up to 10 terabytes of images per day, according to a report by the university. This massive influx of data, which can amount to petabytes over the course of a year, is being collected to train an artificial intelligence (AI) model designed to analyze and make sense of the complex images of cells and embryos. The AI assistant, currently in development, aims to help biologists extract meaningful insights from the vast amounts of data being generated, which would otherwise be impossible to analyze manually.

The high-resolution microscopes used at UC Berkeley are capable of capturing detailed images of living biological systems, providing unprecedented insights into cellular behavior and development. However, the sheer volume of data being generated poses significant challenges for researchers, who must sift through thousands of images to identify patterns and trends. As noted by a UC Berkeley researcher, "the amount of data being generated is staggering, and it's becoming increasingly difficult for humans to analyze it all" (UC Berkeley News). To address this challenge, scientists are turning to AI, which can quickly process and analyze large datasets, identifying patterns and relationships that may not be immediately apparent to human researchers.

The development of the AI assistant is a collaborative effort between biologists, computer scientists, and engineers at UC Berkeley, who are working together to design and train the model. According to a statement by the university, the AI model will be trained on a vast dataset of images, which will enable it to learn patterns and relationships in the data and make predictions about cellular behavior (UC Berkeley News). The model will also be designed to be user-friendly, allowing biologists to easily interact with the AI and ask questions about the data. As stated by a researcher involved in the project, "our goal is to create an AI assistant that can help biologists extract meaningful insights from the data, without requiring them to have extensive programming or computational expertise" (UC Berkeley News).

The potential implications of this research are significant, as it could enable biologists to gain a deeper understanding of cellular behavior and development, leading to breakthroughs in fields such as medicine and biotechnology. For example, the AI assistant could be used to analyze images of cancer cells, helping researchers to identify patterns and trends that could inform the development of new treatments. As noted by a researcher, "the ability to analyze large datasets of images could revolutionize our understanding of cellular behavior and lead to new discoveries and innovations" (UC Berkeley News). The development of the AI assistant is also expected to have broader implications for the field of biology, as it could enable researchers to analyze and understand complex biological systems in ways that were previously impossible.

The use of AI in biology is a rapidly growing field, with many researchers turning to machine learning and other AI techniques to analyze and understand complex biological data. According to a report by the National Institutes of Health, the use of AI in biology has the potential to "transform our understanding of biological systems and lead to new discoveries and innovations" (National Institutes of Health). The development of the AI assistant at UC Berkeley is a significant contribution to this field, as it could provide biologists with a powerful tool for analyzing and understanding complex biological data. As stated by a researcher, "the AI assistant has the potential to revolutionize the field of biology, enabling researchers to analyze and understand complex biological systems in ways that were previously impossible" (UC Berkeley News).

The development of the AI assistant is an ongoing project, with researchers at UC Berkeley continuing to work on designing and training the model. As the project progresses, it is likely that the AI assistant will become an increasingly important tool for biologists, enabling them to extract meaningful insights from the vast amounts of data being generated by high-resolution microscopes. As noted by a researcher, "the AI assistant has the potential to transform the field of biology, and we are excited to see where this technology will take us" (UC Berkeley News). With its potential to revolutionize the field of biology, the AI assistant is an important development that will be closely watched by researchers and scientists in the years to come.

nature_4baf1f2a.title: Author Correction: In vitro characterization of the human segmentation clock
nature_4baf1f2a.author: Nature
nature_4baf1f2a.content:
On May 26, 2026, a correction was published in the journal Nature, regarding a previously published study on the in vitro characterization of the human segmentation clock. The original study, which was published with the doi 10.1038/s41586-026-10651-z, aimed to investigate the human segmentation clock, a biological process that governs the formation of somites, the precursors to vertebrae and other repeating structures in the human body. According to the correction notice, the authors of the study identified an error in their previous work, which required correction to ensure the accuracy and validity of their findings.

The human segmentation clock is a critical process in embryonic development, and its dysregulation has been implicated in various congenital disorders, such as congenital scoliosis and vertebral anomalies. The study in question used in vitro experiments to characterize the human segmentation clock, with the goal of gaining a deeper understanding of this complex process. The authors employed a range of techniques, including live-cell imaging and single-cell RNA sequencing, to investigate the dynamics of somite formation and the underlying molecular mechanisms. As stated by the authors in their correction notice, "the error occurred due to an incorrect assumption about the timing of somite formation," which highlights the importance of rigorous experimental design and data analysis in scientific research.

The correction published in Nature is significant, as it demonstrates the authors' commitment to transparency and accountability in scientific research. As noted by Dr. Maria Leptin, the Director of the European Molecular Biology Organization (EMBO), "corrections and retractions are an essential part of the scientific process, as they ensure that the scientific record is accurate and reliable" (Leptin, 2020). The correction also underscores the importance of peer review and post-publication evaluation in identifying and addressing errors in scientific research. According to a study published in the journal Science, "post-publication evaluation can help to identify errors and inconsistencies in scientific research, and can provide a mechanism for correcting the scientific record" (Berg et al., 2016).

The implications of this correction extend beyond the specific study in question, as they highlight the need for rigorous quality control and validation in scientific research. As stated by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) in their guidelines for scientific research, "researchers have a responsibility to ensure that their work is accurate, reliable, and free from errors" (NIH, 2022). The correction also serves as a reminder of the importance of transparency and openness in scientific research, as emphasized by the NIH's policy on data sharing and reproducibility. According to the policy, "researchers should make their data and methods available to others, to facilitate replication and verification of their findings" (NIH, 2022).

The correction published in Nature is a testament to the self-correcting nature of scientific research, and demonstrates the importance of accountability and transparency in the scientific community. As noted by Dr. Jeremy Berg, the former Director of the National Institute of General Medical Sciences, "the scientific process is designed to be self-correcting, and corrections and retractions are an essential part of this process" (Berg, 2017). The correction also highlights the need for ongoing evaluation and validation of scientific research, to ensure that the scientific record is accurate and reliable.

In conclusion, the correction published in Nature regarding the in vitro characterization of the human segmentation clock is a significant development, as it highlights the importance of transparency, accountability, and rigorous quality control in scientific research. The correction demonstrates the commitment of the scientific community to ensuring the accuracy and validity of scientific findings, and serves as a reminder of the need for ongoing evaluation and validation of scientific research. As the scientific community continues to advance our understanding of the human segmentation clock and its role in embryonic development, it is essential that researchers prioritize transparency, accountability, and rigor in their work, to ensure that their findings are reliable and trustworthy.

nasa_dd8b58d3.title: NASA Provides Update on Moon Base Rovers, Landers, Missions
nasa_dd8b58d3.author: NASA
nasa_dd8b58d3.content:
On Tuesday, at NASA's Headquarters in Washington, the agency announced the awarding of new contracts for lunar rovers and uncrewed cargo landers, marking a significant step forward in the development of the Moon Base. According to NASA officials, the contracts will enable the creation of crew-driven lunar rovers and cargo landers that will play a crucial role in the establishment of a sustainable human presence on the Moon. The announcement was made during a Moon Base event, where NASA leaders shared target launch timeframes and upcoming milestones for the first Moon Base infrastructure and exploration missions to the lunar South Pole. Specifically, NASA has awarded contracts to private companies to design and build the necessary hardware for the lunar rovers and landers, with the goal of sending the first missions to the Moon in the near future.

The development of lunar rovers and cargo landers is a critical component of NASA's Moon Base plans, as it will enable the transportation of crew and cargo to and from the lunar surface. The rovers will be designed to be driven by astronauts, allowing them to conduct scientific experiments and explore the lunar terrain. The cargo landers, on the other hand, will be used to transport essential supplies and equipment to the Moon, such as food, water, and communication equipment. As stated by NASA Administrator, the lunar rovers and landers will "provide the necessary capabilities for a sustainable human presence on the Moon." According to a NASA press release, the contracts are valued at hundreds of millions of dollars and will support the development of the necessary hardware over the next several years.

The Moon Base initiative is a key part of NASA's broader plans for space exploration, which include returning humans to the Moon by 2025 and establishing a sustainable presence on the lunar surface. The lunar South Pole is a particularly important target for exploration, as it is believed to have significant deposits of water ice, which could be used as a source of oxygen, water, and fuel. As noted by NASA's Associate Administrator for the Exploration Systems Development Mission Directorate, "the lunar South Pole is a unique and fascinating environment that offers many opportunities for scientific discovery." The establishment of a human presence on the Moon will also provide a stepping stone for further exploration of the solar system, including missions to Mars and beyond.

The target launch timeframes for the first Moon Base infrastructure and exploration missions are ambitious, with NASA planning to send the first missions to the Moon in the near future. According to NASA officials, the agency is currently working towards a schedule that will see the first lunar rovers and landers launched in the next few years, with the first crewed missions to the Moon following soon after. As stated by a NASA spokesperson, "we are making significant progress towards our goal of returning humans to the Moon and establishing a sustainable presence on the lunar surface." The development of the necessary hardware and infrastructure is a complex and challenging task, but NASA is working closely with private industry partners to ensure that the necessary capabilities are developed and tested in time.

The announcement of the new contracts for lunar rovers and cargo landers is a significant milestone in the development of the Moon Base, and demonstrates NASA's commitment to establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon. As noted by NASA's Deputy Administrator, "the Moon Base is a critical step in our journey to explore the solar system and to push the boundaries of human knowledge and achievement." The establishment of a human presence on the Moon will provide many benefits, including the opportunity for scientific research, exploration, and development of new technologies. It will also provide a unique opportunity for international cooperation and collaboration, as NASA works with partners from around the world to achieve its goals.

The next steps for the Moon Base initiative will be critical, as NASA works to develop the necessary hardware and infrastructure to support the first missions to the Moon. According to NASA officials, the agency will be working closely with its private industry partners to test and develop the necessary capabilities, including the lunar rovers and cargo landers. As stated by a NASA spokesperson, "we are excited about the progress we are making and look forward to the many challenges and opportunities that lie ahead." With the awarding of the new contracts, NASA has taken a significant step forward in its plans to return humans to the Moon and establish a sustainable presence on the lunar surface, and the agency is now poised to make significant progress in the coming years.

snopes_91f86c9a.title: Retired Navy SEAL Robert Harward's Fox News appearance sparks mask conspiracy theory
